title: Home guide: breathing rate and exercise
subject: Science (GCSE Biology, Chemistry, Physics)
source: Written for gcse-science/y10 lesson 28 (Home practical guide and safety card: breathing rate (portal worksheet; gentle stepping only))
intro: Read it all first, then do it with an adult nearby.

practical.aim: Investigate how exercise affects breathing rate.
safety: Stop if you feel unwell, dizzy or very out of breath
An adult knows what you are doing and stays nearby
Clear a space; tidy up and wash your hands afterwards
method: Sit still for 2 minutes. Count your breaths in 1 minute (resting rate). Repeat twice.
Step gently on the bottom stair for 2 minutes.
Count breaths for 1 minute straight away, then each minute until back to resting.
Calculate the mean resting rate and the recovery time.

questions.q: Explain why breathing rate increases during exercise.
questions.a: Muscles respire faster and need more oxygen and to remove more carbon dioxide, so breathing rate and depth increase.
